newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO soft, runs cut spurs some optimism.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO soft, runs cut spurs some optimism.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices remained under pressure on ample supplies but news of Shell refinery cutting runs to 95 percent might stem price slide, traders said on Friday.
They said there were at least two fuel oil cargoes loading from Kuwait in the first half of February seen heading towards the Asia. Traders were uncertain if the cargoes have been committed.
In South Korea, some remaining supplies for end January loading were heard offered in the market. Price indications were unclear.

Amid ample supplies, bidding levels by China have also dropped. Traders said the latest bid by China were heard at $115 per tonne for end January delivery to southern China, c+f for 180-cst supplies, down from $118-$119 a week ago.
There were also talks of unsold stock stored in very large crude carriers (VLCC) outside Chinese waters in the south.
They said these cargoes might still be seeking outlets as Chinese demand remained weak.
But sellers said the saving grace in the market currently could be news of Shell refinery cutting refinery runs by around 30,000 barrels a day starting today.
In the swaps market, prices were largely unchanged. February was indicated at $108.50/$110 against Thursday's $108.50/$110.
